subtopics.title: Grouped Data Revision — Intervals, Histograms and the Estimated Mean

questions.question: The first check on any grouped frequency table is:
options: That the frequencies total n — here 4 + 9 + 17 + 12 + 8 = 50
That every class has the same frequency
That the midpoints are whole numbers
That the modal class comes first

questions.question: Histogram bars must touch because:
options: It saves space on the page
The classes of a continuous measurement share boundaries with no gaps
The frequencies are all positive
The bars are drawn in frequency order

questions.question: The estimated mean of the study-time data is:
options: 37,5 minutes
45,0 minutes
40,8 minutes
41,7 minutes

questions.question: The mean of grouped data is only an ESTIMATE because:
options: The calculator rounds the division
Fifty is too small a sample
The frequencies are approximate
The true values are hidden — each learner is assumed to sit at the class midpoint

questions.question: Frequency polygon points are plotted at:
options: The upper boundary of each class
The lower boundary of each class
The class midpoints, at the height of each frequency
The origin of the axes

questions.question: The polygon is anchored at both ends by:
options: Zeros at the midpoints of the empty classes before the first and after the last
Repeating the first and last frequencies
Vertical lines down from the end points
Joining the last point back to the first

questions.question: The main advantage of a polygon over a histogram is that:
options: It shows the exact data values
It needs no vertical axis
It always looks symmetrical
Two datasets can be compared on one grid without the bars colliding

questions.question: A common polygon-drawing error is:
options: Using straight lines between points
Plotting points at class boundaries instead of midpoints
Labelling the axes
Starting the shape on the horizontal axis

subtopics.title: Ogives — Building the Cumulative Frequency Curve

questions.question: The cumulative frequency column for the study-time data reads:
Ogive points are plotted at:
options: The class midpoints
The lower boundary of each class
The upper boundary of each class, because each total is only complete there
Whole-number values of frequency

questions.question: The extra point that starts the ogive is:
options: The lower boundary of the first class with cumulative count zero — here (0; 0)
The midpoint of the first class with its frequency
The origin, whatever the first class is
The point (15; 15)

questions.question: An ogive can never slope downward because:
options: The axes are always positive
The classes are equal in width
Smooth curves cannot decrease
A running total cannot shrink — the column only ever adds

subtopics.title: Reading the Ogive — Median, Quartiles and Percentiles

questions.question: The median of the 50 study times is read at position:
options: 50 ÷ 2 = 25, giving approximately 41 minutes
50 ÷ 4 = 12,5, giving approximately 29 minutes
Position 30, giving 45 minutes
Position 50, giving 75 minutes

questions.question: The interquartile range of the data is approximately:
options: 41 minutes
75 minutes
54 − 29 = 25 minutes
13 minutes

questions.question: The 90th percentile is found at position:
options: 0,9 × 50 = 45, reading approximately 66 minutes
45 minutes on the horizontal axis

questions.question: To answer 'how many learners study MORE than 55 minutes', you:
options: Read across from 55 on the vertical axis
Multiply 55 by the modal frequency
Read the frequency of the last class only
Go up from 55 to the curve, read about 38 below, and subtract from 50 — about 12

subtopics.title: The Skyline and the Mountain Profile

questions.question: In the skyline picture, each building's height represents:
options: How many learners fall in that class interval
The width of the class
The midpoint of the class
The study time of the best student

questions.question: The buildings share walls because:
options: The city has limited land
Time is continuous — 29 and 31 minutes live in neighbouring classes with a common boundary at 30
The frequencies are consecutive numbers
The classes overlap each other

questions.question: Estimating the mean 'stands every resident in the middle of their building', meaning:
options: The median is used instead of the mean
The tallest building is ignored
Each learner is assumed to sit at the class midpoint before multiplying by frequency
Only the middle class is counted

questions.question: The mountain profile (frequency polygon) beats the skyline when:
options: The data has only one class
The frequencies are very large
Exact values are needed
Two datasets must be compared on the same grid

subtopics.title: The Running Total Tells a Different Story

questions.question: In the tuckshop picture, the histogram and the ogive correspond to:
options: The today column and the total-so-far column
Two copies of the same column
The profit column and the loss column
The stock list and the price list

questions.question: The total 13 belongs at 30 minutes on the ogive because:
options: 30 is the midpoint of the data
13 is close to 15
The running total of 13 is only complete at the END of the second class
The vertical axis starts at 13

questions.question: A steep stretch of the ogive corresponds to:
options: An empty class
A crowded class — the running total grows fastest where data is dense
A drawing error
The interquartile range

questions.question: If your ogive dips downhill anywhere, it means:
options: The data contains negative times
The modal class was skipped
The curve was drawn too smoothly
A subtraction slipped into a column that only ever adds

subtopics.title: Across and Down — Reading Answers off the Curve

questions.question: The two-step reading move on an ogive is:
options: Across from the position on the vertical axis to the curve, then down to the value
Up from the value, then across to the position
Diagonally from the origin
Down from the curve's peak

questions.question: The middle of the line of 50 learners stands at position 25 and reads:
options: Exactly 45 minutes
Approximately 29 minutes
Approximately 41 minutes — the median
Approximately 66 minutes

questions.question: The interquartile range represents:
options: The full spread from fastest to slowest
The span of the middle half of the line, extremes trimmed off
The distance between the two tallest bars
Half of the median

questions.question: Ogive answers must include the word 'approximately' because:
options: The ruler may be inaccurate
Graphs are always wrong
The marker requires three decimal places
The exact values are sealed inside their classes — every reading is an estimate
